Investigate it with code (inspect the columns first) and determine which resource(s) caused the anomalous cost for this account on this date. 5. Answer.

{"resource": [{"name": "<resource name>", "type": "<resource type>"}]}
List every resource that is a root cause; include only root causes.

    sub = acc[acc.cloud_service==cs]

    comp['delta']=comp['anom']-comp['base']

        bi = sub[(sub.date.isin(base_dates))&(sub.instance_family==fam)].num_instances.mean()
        ai = sub[(sub.date==anom)&(sub.instance_family==fam)].num_instances.sum()
        print('   fam',fam,'base inst:',round(bi,1),'anom inst:',ai)
    print()

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP']
anom='2025-10-13'
base_dates=['2025-10-%02d'%d for d in range(6,13)]
# total cost change
tot_base = acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('date').unblended_cost.sum().mean()
tot_anom = acc[acc.date==anom].unblended_cost.sum()
print('total delta:', round(tot_anom-tot_base,1))

# check VFRAe4nYaW and 0sCXpDQUOa across all dates: are they new rows on anom?
for fam in ['VFRAe4nYaW','0sCXpDQUOa']:
    sub = acc[acc.instance_family==fam]
    print(fam, 'csps:', sub.csp.unique(), 'cloud_services:', sub.cloud_service.unique())
    d = sub.groupby('date').agg(cost=('unblended_cost','sum'), inst=('num_instances','sum'))
    print(d.tail(12).to_string())
    # what's the normal day count of rows / instances
    print()
# Also check: on anom, how many total instances vs baseline?
print('baseline total inst/day:', acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('date').num_instances.sum().mean())
print('anom total inst:', acc[acc.date==anom].num_instances.sum())
# which cloud services do these families belong to
print(acc[acc.instance_family.isin(['VFRAe4nYaW','0sCXpDQUOa'])][['date','csp','cloud_service','application']].drop_duplicates().to_string())

{"code": "import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP']
anom='2025-10-13'

print(comp.to_string())
print()

    print('  base instances per fam:', sub[sub.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('instance_family').num_instances.mean().round(1).to_dict())
    print('  anom instances per fam:', sub[sub.date==anom].groupby('instance_family').num_instances.sum().to_dict())
    print()"}

{"code": "import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP']
anom='2025-10-13'
base_dates=['2025-10-%02d'%d for d in range(6,13)]
for cs in ['6K5fR','scSKz','z9l3Q','zxdxb','mESkW','bi1wn','ALEKJ','l5O5g','Jmdc3','ZgEWk','7MZFe']:
    sub = acc[acc.cloud_service==cs]
    b = sub[sub.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('instance_family').unblended_cost.mean()
    a = sub[sub.date==anom].groupby('instance_family').unblended_cost.sum()
    comp = pd.concat({'base':b,'anom':a},axis=1).fillna(0)
    comp['delta']=comp['anom']-comp['base']
    top = comp.nlargest(3,'delta')
    print(cs, 'total delta:', round(comp['delta'].sum(),1), 'top3 share:', round(top['delta'].sum()/comp['delta'].sum(),2))
    print(top.to_string())
    # check instance counts for top families
    for fam in top.index:
        bi = sub[(sub.date.isin(base_dates))&(sub.instance_family==fam)].num_instances.mean()
        ai = sub[(sub.date==anom)&(sub.instance_family==fam)].num_instances.sum()
        print('   fam',fam,'base inst:',round(bi,1),'anom inst:',ai)
    print()"}

{"code": "import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP']
anom='2025-10-13'
base_dates=['2025-10-%02d'%d for d in range(6,13)]
# total cost change
tot_base = acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('date').unblended_cost.sum().mean()
tot_anom = acc[acc.date==anom].unblended_cost.sum()
print('total delta:', round(tot_anom-tot_base,1))

# check VFRAe4nYaW and 0sCXpDQUOa across all dates: are they new rows on anom?
for fam in ['VFRAe4nYaW','0sCXpDQUOa']:
    sub = acc[acc.instance_family==fam]
    print(fam, 'csps:', sub.csp.unique(), 'cloud_services:', sub.cloud_service.unique())
    d = sub.groupby('date').agg(cost=('unblended_cost','sum'), inst=('num_instances','sum'))
    print(d.tail(12).to_string())
    # what's the normal day count of rows / instances
    print()
# Also check: on anom, how many total instances vs baseline?
print('baseline total inst/day:', acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)].groupby('date').num_instances.sum().mean())
print('anom total inst:', acc[acc.date==anom].num_instances.sum())
# which cloud services do these families belong to
print(acc[acc.instance_family.isin(['VFRAe4nYaW','0sCXpDQUOa'])][['date','csp','cloud_service','application']].drop_duplicates().to_string())"}
